The data above is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ compute $P(Z>0.73).$ Use the table above and do not round your answer.

$P(Z>0.73)=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14259374/assets/597125714057269b7adf9c0a2a9bbdde9631cf37bc80518281ab4444c3189717.png)

For a random variable $Z∼N(0,1),$ we have the following symmetry property for $a>0:$

$$
P(Z>a)=P(Z<-a)=Φ(-a)
$$

We're given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(Z>0.73).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14259374/assets/6d98ddf273e1176278fd9d05da5bbe4c073daba99a7cdfadc39d011ac4acc34c.png)

By symmetry, this equals the area corresponding to the probability $P(Z<-0.73).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14259374/assets/28bd59bc3f54997cf4ee9e21de15c3ec3dfe8c5cf6d8194709e9aee2d23b7658.png)

Therefore,

$$
P(Z>0.73)=P(Z<-0.73)=Φ(-0.73)=0.2327.
$$
